request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now have an end date, and all four tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V31__rate_to.sql`, adds an empty-by-default `to_date` column to the rate table.
- **Server:**
  - The rate request, stored rate and response all carry the to-date. A to-date before the from-date is refused with a 400, and nothing is saved or written to the audit file.
  - `RATE_SET` adds ` to=<date>` at the end of the line only when a to-date was given.
  - `Rate.inForce` still picks the rate with the latest from-date on or before the claim's date. If that rate's to-date is before the claim's date, the claim has no rate, so its due is n/a. Every figure (claim due, totals, statements, the late charge) goes through this one function, so they all follow.
- **Front end:**
  - The rate form has a "To" date field (`rate-form-to`), checked for a to-date before the from-date before it is sent.
  - The rate list has a "To" column (`rate-to`).
  - `rateOn` uses the same rule as the server, so every on-screen due and total follows too.

**A rule I had to add.** A person's total used to show n/a whenever their grade had no rate in force today, unless a claim had a fixed figure (settled or bound by a statement) or a figure under another grade. With end dates, that rule makes the first test's total n/a when it expects 3.00: today's rate has ended, but older claims still have figures.

I changed the rule so that a counted claim dated on or before today that still has a figure also keeps the total. Before end dates this couldn't happen, so the only old behaviour that stays different is a claim dated after today. The change is in `Rollup`, `TakeStatement` and `personDueTotal`. It is my reading of what the request means, so check it matches what you intended.
